name: Tehri Dam break (hypothetical)
region: Tehri Garhwal / Pauri Garhwal / Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India
summary: Hypothetical breach of the 260.5 m Tehri earth-and-rockfill dam with the reservoir at FRL, routed over real SRTM terrain down the Bhagirathi past Koteshwar to Devprayag and down the Ganga to Rishikesh.

dem.source: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles, Terrarium encoding, zoom 13 (https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png); SRTM-derived in this region; box-filter area-averaged to 60 m cells
dem.conditioning: 0 void cells filled; 1992 single-cell pits raised to their lowest neighbour (mean 1.8 m, max 32.3 m); minimal-change (L1 isotonic) strictly-descending fit along the traced river path: 1256 of 1568 river-path cells changed by >0.5 m (657 raised, 599 lowered; median |dz| 4.2 m; 157 cells >10 m; max raise 20.4 m, max lowering 21.0 m)

dam.name: Tehri Dam
dam.publishedVolumeSource: Gross storage 3.54 km³ (THDC India figure, as given in Wikipedia "Tehri Dam"); compared with the DEM table at FRL EL 830 m (THDC).

stageStorage.note: Integrated on a 90 m grid resampled from Terrarium z12 tiles over [78.25, 30.3, 78.8, 30.75]: cells hydraulically connected to the reservoir below each level without crossing the dam line (minimax priority flood), volume = Σ(level − ground)·cell area. DEM volume at 830 m = 3.46 km³ vs published 3.54 km³ (-2%); SRTM (Feb 2000) predates impoundment (2006) so the basin is dry in the DEM. Not rescaled. At the initial level the reservoir spans [78.317, 30.363, 78.640, 30.607], which extends OUTSIDE the simulation box (the table still counts it).

breach.note: Froehlich (2008) regression: Bavg = 0.27·k0·Vw^0.32·Hb^0.04 = 378 m, tf = 63.2·√(Vw/(g·Hb²)) = 88.2 min, with k0 = 1 (piping (internal erosion): with the reservoir at FRL 830 m, 9.5 m below the crest, overtopping cannot start the breach), Vw = 3455.2 million m³ (DEM table, initial level 830 m above breach bottom), Hb = 224.2 m (crest − SRTM bed). finalWidth is the bottom width Bavg − z·Hb; side slope 0.7 (H:V, Froehlich 2008 piping). Hb and/or Vw are beyond the range of Froehlich's calibration data, so treat these as order-of-magnitude defaults.

notes: Hypothetical scenario for education and research; not a safety assessment of Tehri Dam, which is a heavily engineered and monitored structure.

The published 260.5 m height with top of dam at 839.5 m implies a base at EL 579 m, below the SRTM river bed (~615 m), i.e. it is measured from foundation level; DamSpec.height here is crest minus the SRTM valley floor just downstream of the dam, as the contract defines it.

SRTM (Feb 2000) predates impoundment (2006), so the reservoir basin is dry terrain in the DEM; the Koteshwar dam and reservoir (commissioned 2011-12) and the partially built Tehri embankment of 2000 are not represented as structures.
Dam axis location: OSM way 93091865 (Tehri Dam) centroid snapped to the highest-accumulation cell within 500 m.

Elevation is SRTM-derived (Feb 2000) surface elevation area-averaged to 60 m: no river bathymetry, and channels narrower than a cell are not resolved (valley floors are biased high where the gorge is narrower than 60 m).

DEM conditioning: 0 void cells filled; 1992 single-cell pits raised to their lowest neighbour (mean 1.8 m, max 32.3 m); minimal-change (L1 isotonic) strictly-descending fit along the traced river path: 1256 of 1568 river-path cells changed by >0.5 m (657 raised, 599 lowered; median |dz| 4.2 m; 157 cells >10 m; max raise 20.4 m, max lowering 21.0 m).
Stage-storage is DEM-integrated (see stageStorage.note); compared, not rescaled, to the published volume.
DamSpec.height = crest 839.5 m − lowest SRTM bed within 700 m downstream of the axis (615.3 m).
Default duration = river path length 109.7 km at an assumed 3 m/s mean front speed, rounded up to whole hours (heuristic, not a prediction).

Populations: OSM population tag where present, otherwise a typical value for the place type (city 100,000, town 10,000, village 1,000, hamlet 150), flagged populationSource "typical" — not a census figure.
basinHandoff: the traced path leaves the box at the outlet point; the flood continues in basin reach ganga_1 of data/ganga/rivers.json.
